title: Sustainable Environmental Communication Project: Eco-Friendly and Sensory Materials for Museums
research_question: To propose a tool for organizing integrated information on so-called smart materials that takes into account both user-centered (perception and involvement) and environment-centered (social and environmental) perspectives for wayfinding design in museums.

participants.description: 63 scientific articles selected through a two-phase systematic literature review; 7 national and international material libraries investigated. Additionally, 'various actors involved in the museum field (superintendents, directors of museums, designers, curators, visitors, employees, and quality certification bodies)' were consulted for identifying best practices.
participants.recruitment: Articles selected by keywords, publication date (since 2004), and content from Web of Science, Scopus, and secondary sources. Material libraries were consulted online.

stimuli_or_exposures.description: 63 scientific articles related to museum wayfinding, environmental accessibility, and sustainability. Online databases of 7 national and international material libraries (Material Design Point, ArTec, Material Connexion, MATto, Materioteca Politecnico di Milano, Materially).

measures.instrument: Keyword search string (Eco-Friendly Materials, Environment-Friendly Materials, Ecological Materials, Sensory Materials, Inclusive Materials); Nature of topic (museum wayfinding, environmental accessibility, sustainability); Publication date (since 2004); Content relevance.

measures.construct: Characteristics of materials in material libraries
measures.instrument: Material properties (communicative, acoustic, olfactory, innovative), environmental performance (impact, certifications), connoting characteristics (accessibility, user experience, modularity/reversibility, sustainability).

measures.construct: Structure and content of the proposed 'standard sheet'
measures.instrument: Integration of technical (sensory, environmental) information, contextualization within wayfinding application cases, macro-objectives for environmental impact, inclusive visual approach.

findings.antecedent: Current literature on museum wayfinding design
findings.consequent: Integrated approach to sustainable and inclusive design
findings.mechanism: Current approaches treat user-centered and environment-centered design separately, leading to a lack of holistic solutions.
findings.quote: A first theoretical result was obtained from the bibliographic research... which highlighted a “sectoral” trend in the design of museum wayfinding.

findings.antecedent: Use of sensorial materials (visual stimuli, auditory stimulation, tactile stimulation, olfactory stimulation) in museum wayfinding
findings.consequent: User well-being, reduced museum fatigue, improved intuitive human-environment interaction, increased visitor numbers
findings.mechanism: Sensory inputs provide useful information, engage users emotionally, and reduce cognitive load, contributing to a positive experience and reducing fatigue.
findings.quote: Emotional design elements can be envisaged by visual stimuli... auditory stimulation... tactile stimulation... and olfactory stimulation...

findings.antecedent: Use of bio-based materials (biodegradable, compostable, recyclable) and react-based materials (integrated with nanotechnologies) in museums
findings.consequent: Environmental sustainability (optimized production, reduced resource consumption, reduced external maintenance/energy dependence)
findings.mechanism: These materials inherently have properties that reduce environmental footprint and operational costs.
findings.quote: Bio-based materials: inspired by biological systems... React-based materials: integrated with nanotechnologies functional to the activation of self-regulation processes...

findings.consequent: Integrated material selection for wayfinding projects
findings.mechanism: Materials are often searchable by raw material or application, not by connoting properties relevant to usability or environmental impact, and technical data is often empirical rather than quantitative.
findings.quote: information on their environmental impact and sustainability is not explicitly declared... The filing also includes the perceptive and sustainability characteristics, which can be traced separately...

findings.antecedent: Use of the proposed 'standard sheet' for material cataloging
findings.consequent: Informed material selection for museum wayfinding projects (balancing aesthetic-perceptual performance and environmental impact)
findings.mechanism: By providing a structured, comprehensive, and visually organized overview of material properties (sensory, environmental, technical) and application contexts, the sheet reduces cognitive load for designers and enables holistic decision-making.
findings.quote: The final step of the research involved the development of a "standard sheet" for the cataloging of materials in material libraries according to technical-perceptive-environmental data...

findings.antecedent: Standard sheet's inclusion of six environmental macro-objectives
findings.consequent: Sustainable material choices in wayfinding projects
findings.mechanism: Explicitly defining and linking materials to these objectives provides a clear framework for evaluating and selecting environmentally responsible options.
findings.quote: six project macro-objectives were defined: minimization of material resources... choice of resources and processes with a low environmental impact...

findings.antecedent: Standard sheet's inclusive visual approach (balanced visual and textual code, structured information)
findings.consequent: Improved cognitive processing, understanding of material information, better decision-making for inclusive design
findings.mechanism: Visual organization reduces cognitive load and facilitates rapid comprehension of complex, heterogeneous information, making the tool more accessible and effective.
findings.quote: The material filing repertoire was designed with the aim of facilitating the use of the information contained within using the principles of information visualization... to achieve a different communicative effectiveness...

mechanisms: Current approaches treat user-centered and environment-centered design separately, leading to a lack of holistic solutions.
Sensory inputs provide useful information, engage users emotionally, and reduce cognitive load, contributing to a positive experience and reducing fatigue.
Bio-based and react-based materials inherently have properties that reduce environmental footprint and operational costs.

Materials are often searchable by raw material or application, not by connoting properties relevant to usability or environmental impact, and technical data is often empirical rather than quantitative.

By providing a structured, comprehensive, and visually organized overview of material properties (sensory, environmental, technical) and application contexts, the sheet reduces cognitive load for designers and enables holistic decision-making.
Explicitly defining and linking materials to environmental macro-objectives provides a clear framework for evaluating and selecting environmentally responsible options.
Visual organization reduces cognitive load and facilitates rapid comprehension of complex, heterogeneous information, making the tool more accessible and effective.
implementation_implications: Designers can use the standard sheet to select materials for museum wayfinding projects that balance aesthetic-perceptual performance and environmental impact, promoting inclusion and sustainability.
The tool provides information on alternative communication channels for diverse users and quantitative environmental impact properties.
The proposed material filing system can be integrated into BIM environments for digital design processes, creating interoperable material libraries.

Stakeholders (public clients, museum directors, exhibition curators, designers, financiers) can use this tool to improve interaction during the design phase and promote more accessible and sustainable museums.

tables.description: Keyword identification and eligibility criteria used for the systematic literature review.
Participant list for material libraries survey, including name, link, and operational profile.

limitations: The information on analyzed materials is sparse and fragmented across multiple, heterogeneous data sources (relational databases, text files).
The current stage involves testing prototypes of the standard sheets with museum designers and stakeholders to gather feedback, implying the tool is not yet fully validated or implemented.
The study focuses on the structuring of information and the proposal of a tool, rather than empirical testing of its impact on design outcomes or user experience.

paper_metadata.title: Sustainable Environmental Communication Project: Eco-Friendly and Sensory Materials for Museums
paper_metadata.crossref_title: Sustainable Environmental Communication Project: Eco-Friendly and Sensory Materials for Museums
paper_metadata.crossref_abstract: In the context of large museum centers, numerous national and international methodological experiments show the need to consider, in wayfinding design, both the intangible issues of experience arising from perception and involvement (user-centered design), and social and environmental issues (environment-centered design). The aim of this research is to propose a tool for organizing integrated information on so-called smart materials that takes both perspectives into account. This study was performed by conducting a two-phase systematic literature and library review of materials. Specifically, 63 scientific articles—selected by keywords, publication date and content—and 7 national and international material libraries were investigated. The investigation highlighted how the sensory characteristics of wayfinding materials in museums are treated separately from the environmental characteristics and how the quality of the technical information of the materials filed in the material libraries could be improved. The result of the research concerns the structuring of a ‘standard sheet’ for the cataloguing of materials that integrates technical (sensory and environmental) information while also offering a contextualization of the material within wayfinding application cases in known museums. The proposed tool facilitates designers in the selection of materials to be adopted in the wayfinding project, offering information both on their ability to offer alternative communication channels in response to different users’ sense–perceptual functioning and on their quantitative environmental impact properties. This study conducted through the integration of different multidisciplinary fields (technological approach to design, inclusive design, environmental psychology, material science, visual communication, environmental protection related to people’s well-being) offers a significant contribution in the context of museum wayfinding design, providing stakeholders with practical tools to select materials that promote inclusion and sustainability.
